chapter: N'goma drums and the scrapbook clippings
title: Hobby Lobby, Major Bowes and the Goldkette gong
summary: Hutto recalls Morehouse's 1938 appearance on Hobby Lobby with the N'goma drums and on Major Bowes's Capitol Theater hour; a gong from Charlie Horvath sounds.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Back a little earlier in the thirties, about 1938, about the time he was making the splash with the N'goma drums, he was with Dave Ellman on Hobby Lobby. And he
has a certificate that shows that he appeared on the program and part of the script.
Hobby Lobby, okay. What is Hobby Lobby?
As I recall, it's a show that people came on that a little unusual occupation and maybe people tried to guess what they were doing. And of course the N'goma drums were a little different.
I see. This was in the thirties. This is before...

In '38, this was before the war. And he also played I think appeared with Major Bowes on the Capitol. He had the Amateur Hour and then he had on Sundays, the Capitol Theater Hour and Chauncey appeared on that.
That's the gong from the Goldkette band. Charles Horvath gave that to him.
